name: RTL-SDR/LoRa/GPS/RTC hat for Raspberry Pi
one_line: Raspberry Pi HAT combining an RTL2832U+R860 SDR receiver, SX1262 LoRa radio, GPS/GNSS, and RTC on one board.
why_notable: All-in-one SDR/LoRa/GPS expansion board for turning a Raspberry Pi into a portable signal-monitoring platform.

name: MSI.SDR 10kHz-2GHz Panadapter SDR Receiver
one_line: 12-bit ADC SDR receiver covering 10kHz-2GHz with up to 10MHz bandwidth, 0.5ppm TCXO, SMA antenna port, micro-USB, aluminium enclosure.
why_notable: Wideband receiver in a different product line from the tracked RTL-SDR, HackRF, KrakenSDR and PlutoSDR. An RSP1 clone - worth stating plainly.

name: Mini RTL-SDR Dongle
one_line: USB-C RTL2832U+R860 SDR receiver, 100kHz-1.74GHz, in a CNC aluminum case with TCXO and switchable 5V bias tee.
why_notable: Compact, aluminum-housed RTL-SDR variant with bias tee and HF direct sampling not covered by the existing RTL-SDR Blog V4 entry.

name: RTL-SDR
one_line: Generic RTL2832U/R820T USB TV-tuner dongle repurposed as a wideband (24-1850MHz) software-defined radio receiver for GNU Radio/SDR#.
why_notable: Entry-level SDR receiver distinct from the RTL-SDR Blog V4 already tracked (no TCXO/bias-tee/branding).

name: SDR-Rx Up Converter Module
one_line: HF upconverter and preamp (10kHz-50MHz, relay-switched VHF/UHF/SHF pass-through) extending the low-frequency range of an existing RTL-SDR dongle; F and BNC connectors, USB powered.
why_notable: Adds real HF reception to existing SDR dongles but is an accessory rather than a standalone tool.

name: URTI (Universal Radio Test Instrument)
one_line: In-development wideband full-duplex SDR with an integrated directional coupler, intended to act as spectrum analyzer, VNA, vector signal generator/analyzer, antenna analyzer, power meter and frequency counter in one device.
why_notable: Open-source GSG project (ARDC/TAPR funded) with a live product page, no price and no release. Needs a status check before listing.

name: PandwaRF Marauder
one_line: Autonomous covert RF/remote-control signal capture ('dead-drop') device integrating with the PandwaRF ecosystem for rolling/fixed-code analysis, decryption and generation.
why_notable: High-end professional sub-GHz signals-intelligence device above $1,000, now explicitly in scope; distinct from the already-tracked PandwaRF Rogue Pro.

name: Glytch Mesh Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: LoRa mesh-networking add-on for the WiFi Pineapple Pager enabling decentralized, off-grid messaging between units (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Gives the WiFi Pineapple Pager a sub-GHz LoRa mesh comms channel independent of WiFi/cellular infrastructure.

name: Nibble Zero
one_line: ESP32-S3 + LoRa mesh node (Meshtastic, Meshcore, or Reticulum firmware) with a 3D-printed case and BMP280 sensor that can be flashed and operated directly from a Flipper Zero.
why_notable: Notable for direct Flipper Zero integration — the Flipper flashes and controls the node — bridging an already-cataloged device (Flipper Zero) into LoRa mesh networking; same comms-vs-attack-tool borderline reasoning as the other Nibble variants.

name: Glytch Mesh Mod for Pager
one_line: 3D-printed add-on with an 868/900 MHz radio and integrated antenna that clips onto the WiFi Pineapple Pager for sub-GHz mesh networking.
why_notable: Adds off-grid mesh comms to an already-tracked device. Seen at $79 and $85.32 elsewhere.

name: Nibble Screen Connect
one_line: ESP32-S3 board with a Semtech SX1262 LoRa radio, OLED screen, 2 buttons and a BME280 sensor, breadboard-compatible, for a hand-held Meshtastic or Meshcore mesh node.
why_notable: More expandable open-source Nibble variant (adds Meshcore support alongside Meshtastic); same borderline reasoning as the base Nibble — it's mesh comms hardware, not an attack tool.

name: Flipper Add-on SubGhz
one_line: Flipper Zero GPIO add-on board extending sub-GHz (CC1101-class) radio capability.
why_notable: Third-party sub-GHz extension board for the Flipper Zero from a known hardware-security vendor.

name: Daeva
one_line: DIY PCB: ESP32-WROOM-32U + CC1101 (315/433MHz) with rotary encoder and SD slot for scanning, copying and replaying sub-GHz signals. No assembled unit sold.

name: LoRa Radio Backpack for USB & Bluetooth Nuggets (RFM95)
one_line: RFM95 LoRa radio add-on board (selectable 868MHz or 915MHz) that plugs onto a USB Nugget or Bluetooth Nugget for long-range wireless, exposing UART/SPI/I2C for extra peripherals.
why_notable: Vendor explicitly markets this as enabling 'long-range bad USB attacks' — it's sold specifically to extend the range/reach of the already-listed USB/Bluetooth Nugget BadUSB devices, plus adds Meshtastic support.

name: 2 PCS CC1101 Module with SMA Antenna Transceiver Module (433/315/868/915MHz)
one_line: CC1101-chipset sub-GHz transceiver breakout board with SMA antenna, tunable across 300-348/387-464/779-928MHz, sold as a 2-pack.
why_notable: CC1101 external modules are one of the most common third-party sub-GHz accessories for Flipper Zero/Arduino sub-GHz replay and range-extension projects, corroborated by multiple independent (Tindie, blog) sources beyond this marketplace listing.

name: RFQuack
one_line: Scriptable Python-shell firmware for sniffing, analysing and transmitting sub-GHz and 2.4GHz (nRF24) signals on ESP32/Teensy + CC1101/RF69 hardware.
why_notable: 345 stars, last commit 2024-12-23. Backed by an academic paper.
